summary: HTTPS on node1:8443 is live, serving a certificate issued by a local CA, with a systemd timer that automatically renews the leaf cert before expiry and gracefully reloads nginx to pick it up without dropping connections. However, this turn was force-ended before I could capture direct evidence of a live renewal occurring while under continuous request load, and before running the mandatory per-node restart/reboot evidence protocol. Task is not complete.
actions_performed: Installed nginx on node1 via dnf
Created a local CA (/etc/pki/local-ca/ca.key, ca.crt) on node1

Wrote /usr/local/bin/renew-cert.sh: issues a 6-minute-lived leaf cert (CN=node1, SAN=DNS:node1,IP:$NODE_IP) signed by the local CA whenever less than 3 minutes of validity remain, using openssl x509 -not_before/-not_after for exact short lifetimes; sets nginx-readable ownership/permissions; runs 'nginx -t' then 'systemctl reload nginx' (graceful reload that keeps serving existing connections) after a successful renewal
Configured /etc/nginx/conf.d/https-8443.conf to terminate TLS on port 8443 using /etc/nginx/tls/server.crt and server.key
Ran renew-cert.sh once to produce the initial certificate and fixed file/directory ownership (nginx:nginx) so the nginx worker can read the key/cert under SELinux enforcing mode
Enabled and started nginx; verified curl -k https://$NODE_IP:8443/ returns HTTP 200 over TLSv1.3
Installed and started systemd units cert-renew.service and cert-renew.timer (OnBootSec=30s, OnUnitActiveSec=30s) so the renewal check runs automatically every 30 seconds

Started a background watch script on node1 (/tmp/watch.sh) that curls the HTTPS endpoint every 5 seconds and records the served certificate serial, intended to demonstrate continuous availability across an automatic renewal/reload cycle

Attempted to wait several minutes (cert lifetime is 6 minutes, renewal threshold is 3 minutes remaining) for a live renewal to occur and be captured by the watch log, but discovered background sleep jobs from prior tool calls are not tracked by 'wait' in a freshly-invoked shell, so intended wall-clock waits did not actually elapse; a corrective background sleep was started but the turn was force-ended before it completed or could be checked
Did not yet perform the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol (boot-identity capture, reboot, boot-identity change verification, and post-restart service/data recovery proof) for node1

evidence.requirement: HTTPS serving on port 8443 with a valid certificate
evidence.summary: nginx was enabled/started and is active; curl -vk https://$NODE_IP:8443/ completed a TLSv1.3 handshake and returned HTTP 200 OK with body 'ok'

evidence.requirement: Certificate is issued by a local CA and readable by the service under SELinux
evidence.summary: Local CA created (ca.key/ca.crt); renew-cert.sh issued the initial leaf cert with correct nginx:nginx ownership and 640/644 perms so nginx (SELinux enforcing) can read it

evidence.requirement: Automatic renewal mechanism exists and reloads the service without dropping connections
evidence.summary: renew-cert.sh (checks remaining validity, reissues via openssl with explicit -not_before/-not_after, then runs 'nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx') was installed and wired to a systemd timer (cert-renew.timer, 30s interval) which was enabled and confirmed active

evidence.requirement: Live proof of a renewal occurring while the service keeps answering requests (not yet captured)
evidence.summary: A background curl-every-5s watch loop was started and showed continuous HTTP 200 responses with the initial cert serial (6A9B8848), but the intended multi-minute wait to observe the automatic renewal swap the serial did not actually elapse due to a background-sleep/wait tracking issue across separate tool calls, so the renewal event itself was not yet captured in evidence

evidence.requirement: Mandatory per-node restart protocol (boot identity, reboot, recovery)
evidence.summary: Only baseline node inspection was captured (OS, root access, NODE_IP); no boot-id baseline, reboot, or post-reboot verification has been performed yet for node1
